claims.statement: dcode normally launches an interactive terminal session, while `-n` performs one headless task and `--acp` serves ACP over standard input and output.
Interactive and headless operation start a temporary loopback LangGraph server, wait for its graph, bind a RemoteAgent to the workspace, and tear the subprocess down on failed startup or normal exit.
Headless execution creates a new thread, gates shell access through the shell allow-list, and uses exit 124 when its turn or timeout budget expires.
A workspace binding is durably validated by the server before graph execution; policy drift is rejected, while runtime-only identity changes rebuild the runtime.

Model retry middleware retries transient model-node failures without rerunning completed tool calls, uses per-request model retry settings, and re-raises a terminal provider failure instead of returning it as an AI response.
Correlated retry and model-attempt stream events enable TUI and headless clients to reconcile tentative state and visibly distinguish partial streamed output from a replayed response.

TUI resume selects the most-recent or named thread subject to configured age policy, handles missing threads and database errors by falling back to a fresh session, and can offer a stored-working-directory switch.
ACP runs independently from the temporary RemoteAgent server session, constructing its own model, MCP tools, SQLite checkpointer, and ACP agent context.
Development debug mode preserves the server log and attaches a per-thread client log, while the in-app debug console remains available when secure file logging cannot be used.
Focused tests cover CLI launch dispatch and limits, TUI startup and resume, workspace and offload HTTP guards, remote offload cancellation, and retry streaming behavior.

Interactive startup resolves a displayable model identity before provider construction, defers server startup when credentials are absent, and passes resolved model, policy, sandbox, and MCP options to the server-backed TUI session.
Workspace refusal diagnostics persist and report only an allowlisted bounded policy snapshot; they exclude paths, credentials, environment values, model details, prompts, and profile overrides.

MCP login uses the same source discovery and trust filtering as runtime loading: explicit config is loaded directly, while discovered project servers require applicable trust and persisted approval policy.
Server-owned offload serializes each thread, refuses active, interrupted, pending, unbound, or changed checkpoints, and permits commits only to allowlisted state channels rather than messages.

When cancelled while awaiting offload, RemoteAgent requests server-side cancellation and waits for a terminal operation status; a handoff summarizes a source without compacting it and can seed a new bound thread.

CLI model parameters must be JSON objects, take precedence over configured provider values, and cannot control provider-native retries because dcode owns the retry budget through `--max-retries` or configuration.
Reasoning effort choices are derived from a reasoning-capable model profile; Anthropic models in `between_tools` thinking mode expose only low, medium, and high effort levels.

MCP middleware normalizes empty optional string arguments, converts timeout into a warning that retrying may duplicate server-side work, and turns detected expired authentication into an actionable tool error.
Session cost is graph-owned and checkpointed; it streams an absolute cumulative `session_cost` event so clients render the total without maintaining their own lifetime accounting.

The TUI reads `warnings.session_cost_threshold_usd` as a per-thread soft limit, opens an acknowledgement-only warning only on the first strictly over-threshold total, and marks a restored above-threshold thread as already warned.

The SubagentPanel renders validated main-agent custom-stream lifecycle events by `js_eval` phase, preserves user expansion and phase selection semantics across events, and finalizes unfinished rows as cancelled when a turn is interrupted.
Subagent panel text from model-authored JavaScript is sanitized and bounded before plain Textual rendering, preventing control, terminal-escape, bidi, and markup content from changing the display.

The system-prompt smoke test captures the complete first system message for reproducible interactive and headless runs, normalizes machine-specific values, and asserts that headless mode does not receive unreachable user-question guidance.
